item.text:
Turn complete. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

Two substantive things this turn, plus one important handoff fix.

I closed the last documentation-vs-behavior check by reading `config.go`'s field docs, `ReloadableConfig.apply`/`fromConfig`, `DefaultConfig`, and the version constants. Everything matches upstream and its own documentation: `DefaultConfig` (Heartbeat/Election 1000ms, Commit 50ms, MaxAppendEntries 64, TrailingLogs 10240, SnapshotInterval 120s, SnapshotThreshold 8192, LeaderLeaseTimeout 500ms), `ProtocolVersion` 0..3, `SnapshotVersion` 0..1, and the reloadable subset restricted to the five documented fields. No mismatch.

More importantly, I caught a handoff problem: the brief states `work/.runtime` is **disposable and removed at cleanup**, yet all my evidence logs lived there — they would have vanished. I copied the complete evidence set (all suite/flake logs, the goroutine dump `stall_dump.txt`, control and timing runs, and the three harness logs) to a durable `work/audit-evidence/` directory, and updated the report's artifact section with the `.runtime/<name>` → `audit-evidence/<name>` mapping so a re-reviewer uses the surviving paths. I also added a short report map at the top, since the sections accumulated chronologically, and listed the six `zz_audit_*` diagnostic files with their build-tag gate.

The report is now self-contained and its status line reads COMPLETE.

Final deliverable state:

- Finding 1 (confirmed, low severity): `testing.go`'s `EnsureSamePeers` snapshots its reference peer set once, outside the retry loop, so tests that verify peers after a configuration change can fail on a fully consistent cluster. Confirmed in two shipped tests (`TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3` ~6/20, `TestRaft_HasExistingState` 1/3), reproduced against a 0/20 refresh-each-poll control, and mechanism-verified two ways (goroutine dump showing all nodes already converged, and a propagation-lag study showing node 0 is stale at the first read 15% of the time with otherwise microsecond-scale lag).
- No consensus-level defect: full source review of the root module plus five independent behavioral methods (~16k acked commands across three partition/snapshot/mixed-version harnesses), all clean.
- One open item, honestly flagged as unanswerable offline: whether the one-line frozen-snapshot pattern is the injected mutation or a latent upstream flake — no trustworthy upstream reference is obtainable without network, and the module cache's sumdb records don't verify.
